question: How many cities were initially included under the Smart Cities Mission launched by the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India on **25 June 2015** under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
 
• Initially, **100 cities** were selected to be developed as part of the mission.
 
• The mission aims to improve urban infrastructure and provide better quality of life through **sustainable and inclusive development**.
 
• The cities were selected through a competitive process known as the **Smart Cities Challenge**.
 
• The total planned investment for the mission is estimated at **₹2.05 lakh crore**, covering projects like affordable housing, urban mobility, and IT connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission Objectives:**

 
 
• The mission focuses on **area-based development** such as retrofitting, redevelopment, and greenfield projects.
 
• It emphasizes **smart solutions** like smart meters, intelligent traffic management, and e-governance.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The cities were selected through a **three-stage competition** involving state governments, urban local bodies, and central government evaluation.
 
• Only cities that meet specified criteria are granted funding under the mission.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• Each selected city sets up a **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** for implementation, with support from government and private partners.
 
• The SPV is responsible for planning, appraising, and executing projects under the mission.
 
 
 
• **Progress:**
 
 
• As of 2023, over 7,000 projects have been tendered, with many nearing completion across various cities.
 
• Key focus areas include **urban mobility, affordable housing, and green energy initiatives**.
